subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the points (1,2,3), (2,3,1) and (3,1,2) form an equilateral triangle.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.84 — VSAQ chapter 15 3-D Coordinates, answer 100.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you compute, and what makes the triangle equilateral.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the three distances
steps.margin_note: First mark. Take the three points in pairs and apply the distance formula, which in three dimensions carries a third squared difference. Leave every answer in surd form.
steps.memory_tip: All three come to √6 — the same three numbers 1, 1, 4 in a different order each time.

recall.must_convey: That the three pairwise distances AB, BC and AC are computed with the 3D distance formula.
accept: compute all three distances with the three dimensional distance formula
root of x difference squared plus y difference squared plus z difference squared
find A B, B C and A C
apply the distance formula three times

steps.why: Both questions on this page are answered by computing the SAME three distances. Only the conclusion drawn from them differs, which is why the book prints the note 'Questioning is different but Answering is similar' underneath.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the third squared difference and using the 2D formula.
Simplifying a surd wrongly, which hides the pattern in the three answers.

steps.label: Compare them for equality
steps.margin_note: Second mark. All three distances come out the SAME, which is the definition of an equilateral triangle. Nothing further needs computing.
steps.memory_tip: All three EQUAL is the definition of equilateral. Nothing further needs computing.

lines.text: Hence, A, B, C form an equilateral triangle

recall.must_convey: That all three distances are equal to √6, so the triangle is equilateral.
accept: all three distances are root six so the triangle is equilateral
A B equals B C equals A C
the three sides are the same length

steps.why: Equal distances is the whole definition — no angles need finding, which is what keeps this to two marks.
common_mistakes: Checking only two of the three distances.
Concluding isosceles when all three match.

insider_note: All three distances have to be worked out and shown equal — checking only two proves isosceles, not equilateral. Each comes to √6 from a different arrangement of 1, 1 and 4.
